names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 29 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Ιωάννης ο Νάννος από τη Θεσσαλονίκη», with the rank word left off.

The by-name the same page prints and explains: he was called Ιωάννης because he was born on the eve of the Nativity of the Forerunner, and «για να διακρίνεται όμως από τον πατέρα του, τον φώναζαν Νάννο» — to tell him from his father, who was also John, they called him Nannos.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 29. мај ст. ст., „Свети мученик Нан (Јован) Солунски“ — Свети is not a rank and мученик is the `martyr` this corpus puts in `types`. **The parenthesis is left out and that is the standing rule, not a choice**: one `sr` form per folder, the fullest, and a name given in parenthesis beside another is not a fuller form of it. Dropping „(Јован)“ leaves „Нан … Солунски“ contiguous in the heading, which is the form stored. **The second name is not lost**: this folder already holds both Greek forms, «Ιωάννης» and «Νάννος», off saint.gr, so the pair is recorded and only the `sr` row is single. **Measured**: `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for «Нан Солунски» and for the bare «Нан» as well, so no fold is entered either way; Солунски is kept because the heading prints it and it distinguishes him.

death.note: saint.gr: «Έτσι, στις 29 Μαΐου του 1802 μ.Χ. και ημέρα Πέμπτη, ο Ιωάννης οδηγήθηκε στο Σοάν Παζάρι, τόπο των θανατικών εκτελέσεων.» The same page dates his feigned apostasy to «στις 3 Μαΐου του 1802 μ.Χ.» and his confession to «στις 25 Μαΐου και ημέρα Κυριακή» of the same year. It gives no year of birth.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 29ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Ιωάννης ο Νάννος από τη Θεσσαλονίκη»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 29 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and the day is the day of his beheading. He is none of the Johns the corpus keeps: a shoemaker's son of Thessalonica who worked at Smyrna and was put to death there in 1802. The page also lists him under «Σύναξη των Αγίων Νεομαρτύρων των μετά την άλωση της Κωνσταντινουπόλεως μαρτυρησάντων», the synaxis of the new martyrs after the fall of the City, which is a heading and names nobody on this page. No hymn is printed for him.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 11.06.2026 (29. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Нан (Јован) Солунски“

attestations.note: The day’s sixth entry, on the same menologion 29/5 the Greek row already carries, and one sentence long. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of the 23 to 29 May is. **ONE SENTENCE, AND EVERY WORD OF IT CORROBORATES AN `attested` RECORD.** „Пострадао за веру од Турака 1802. године у Смирни“ — he suffered for the faith at the hands of the Turks in the year 1802 at Smyrna. This folder holds `death` 1802 with `basis: "attested"`, and saint.gr gives both the year and Smyrna. **So `dates` is untouched: there is nothing to widen, nothing to narrow, and an `attested` year is not improved by a second book agreeing with it.** **That is the whole value of this row and it is worth having**: a second calendar, in a third language, independently keeping the same man on the same day with the same year and the same city. `new-martyr` and `martyr` are both corroborated. **THE PARENTHESIS IN THE HEADING IS THE SECOND NAME, AND THE FOLDER ALREADY HOLDS BOTH IN GREEK.** „Нан (Јован)“ against saint.gr’s two separate forms «Ιωάννης» and «Νάννος». Nothing was reconciled and no form was composed; see the name note. **Nobody in the entry gains a row**, it naming only the Turks. `related` stays at `nikephoros-of-chios`, who wrote his account and is the Greek page’s. No `locations`, although Smyrna is named in both books. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
